key_insight: Non-contact air-coupled ultrasound plus AI can infer full cheese texture behavior from images, closing part of the measurement gap between dairy and plant-based cheeses without destroying the sample.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid, one-minute, at-line screening of formulations and quality control for texture optimization in food materials discovery.
method: Imaged 13 commercial cheeses with through-transmission air-coupled ultrasound at 100 kHz.
Converted scans into paired amplitude and time-of-flight C-scan images.
Trained a compact CNN to predict full true stress-strain curves from unseen slices.
evidence_signal: The study used 119 slices and 357 scans, and the model generalized across all 13 products without product-specific calibration.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated on a limited set of commercial cheeses, so broader validation is needed before routine industrial deployment.
paper_title: Sounds Cheesy - Bridging the Texture Gap Between Dairy and Plant-Based cheese with Non-Contact Ultrasound and AI
